## What F02 establishes

F02 asks whether high and low responders differ across the whole proteome, not
just protein by protein. The answer is no: every global test — the proteome
state, the size of the training and acute response, and its direction and spread —
comes back null. The only HR-vs-LR signal is protein-specific, and even that is a
list of exploratory leads that no protein clears at FDR. So the honest headline is
a **shared global response with protein-specific leads**, stated at the scale the
data actually support.

```{r setup}
source(here::here("05_Figures", "F02_proteome", "a_script", "setup.R"))
panel <- function(letter) {
  dir <- here::here("05_Figures", "F02_proteome", "a_script", "panels")
  f <- list.files(dir, pattern = paste0("^panel_", tolower(letter), "_.*\\.R$"), full.names = TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(f) == 1)
  source(f)
}
```

## Panel A — global proteome state (PERMANOVA)

PERMANOVA asks whether two groups' clouds sit in different places in proteome
space, comparing the distance between group centroids to a null built by shuffling
the labels. Two cautions drive the design: it can be fooled by a difference in
*spread* rather than location (checked by PERMDISP in the supplement), and repeated
measures must be respected. So timepoint permutes *within* subject, and the group
test collapses each subject to their mean and treats subjects as the unit, so the
partial subjects cannot act as unequal blocks.

```{r panel-a}
panel("A")
pA
```

Groups overlap (p = `r sprintf("%.2f", perm_group[["Pr(>F)"]][1])`); timepoint does
separate (p = `r sprintf("%.2f", perm_time[["Pr(>F)"]][1])`) — everyone moves
with training, the responder split just isn't a global axis.

## Panel B — response magnitude (RRPP)

RRPP (randomised residual permutation) is the valid permutation scheme when
proteins far outnumber subjects. Here it tests one number per subject: the length
of their before→after change vector, ‖Δ‖. If HR truly "respond more," their ‖Δ‖
should be larger.

```{r panel-b}
panel("B")
pB
```

It isn't (training p = `r sprintf("%.2f", mag_stat$p[1])`, acute p = `r sprintf("%.2f", mag_stat$p[2])`). HR and LR move about equally far.

## Panel C — protein-specific divergence leads

The correct test of "does this protein change differently in HR vs LR" is the
Group × Timepoint interaction, not the overlap of two separate hit lists (Gelman &
Stern 2006). The panel plots each protein's HR change against its LR change;
off-diagonal points are candidates flagged by the interaction pi-gate.

The pi-gate is `p^|log2FC|`, a fold-change-weighted p-value (Xiao 2014, Eq. 2). It
controls no error rate. Under BH it is unforgiving:

```{r pi-vs-fdr}
int_counts <- function(ph) {
  p <- dep_df[[paste0("P.Value_", ph, "_Interaction")]]
  q <- dep_df[[paste0("adj.P.Val_", ph, "_Interaction")]]
  pi <- dep_df[[paste0("sig_pi_", ph, "_Interaction")]]
  data.frame(
    phase = ph,
    raw_p_lt_05 = sum(p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    pi_gated = sum(pi != 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    bh_lt_05 = sum(q < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_q = round(min(q, na.rm = TRUE), 3)
  )
}
int_tbl <- rbind(int_counts("Training"), int_counts("Acute"))
pi_off_p <- vapply(c("Training", "Acute"), function(ph) {
  p <- dep_df[[paste0("P.Value_", ph, "_Interaction")]]
  pi <- dep_df[[paste0("sig_pi_", ph, "_Interaction")]]
  gated <- !is.na(pi) & pi != 0
  100 * sum(gated & p >= 0.05, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(gated)
}, numeric(1))
knitr::kable(int_tbl)
```

The pi-gate is no stricter than raw p (`r int_tbl$pi_gated[1]` vs `r int_tbl$raw_p_lt_05[1]`,
`r int_tbl$pi_gated[2]` vs `r int_tbl$raw_p_lt_05[2]`), and **zero proteins
survive FDR** (minimum q ≈ `r sprintf("%.2f", min(int_tbl$min_q))`–`r sprintf("%.2f", max(int_tbl$min_q))`).
So the divergent points are exploratory
leads, not discoveries; the panel prints both counts so the distinction is visible.
An error-rate-controlled alternative with an effect-size floor is `limma::treat()`.

```{r panel-c}
panel("C")
pC
```

## Panels D–F — the proteome overview

Descriptive scale for the figure. **D** counts DEPs per contrast as a percent of
the proteome against a chance line; **E** shows each contrast's log2FC density; **F**
runs preranked GO GSEA per contrast, collapsing redundant sets, and is the only
FDR-controlled panel. F's acute bout is lopsided toward HR, but read that as a
per-contrast count, not a between-group difference test.

```{r panels-def}
panel("D")
panel("E")
panel("F")
go_tot <- aggregate(cbind(Up, Down) ~ contrast, go_counts, sum) |>
  within(total <- Up + Down)
acute_go <- setNames(go_tot$total, go_tot$contrast)[c("Acute_HR", "Acute_LR")]
pD
pE
pF
```

In the acute bout that asymmetry is `r acute_go[["Acute_HR"]]` non-redundant GO
sets in HR against `r acute_go[["Acute_LR"]]` in LR — two separate counts, not a
tested difference.

## Supplements — the rest of the null argument

Two supplements corroborate "no global divergence" with subjects as the unit. The
**dispersion** supplement uses PERMDISP (distance to the group centroid per
timepoint) to check responders aren't simply more heterogeneous — they aren't
(p = `r sprintf("%.2f", disp_p$pval[1])` / `r sprintf("%.2f", disp_p$pval[2])` / `r sprintf("%.2f", disp_p$pval[3])`). The **direction** supplement runs RRPP on the full
per-subject change matrix and the angle between the groups' mean change vectors —
no directional difference either (p = `r sprintf("%.2f", dir_stat$p[1])` / `r sprintf("%.2f", dir_stat$p[2])`).

```{r supplements}
source(here::here("05_Figures", "F02_proteome", "a_script", "panels", "panel_c_divergence.R"))
source(here::here("05_Figures", "F02_proteome", "a_script", "panels", "panel_b_trajectory.R"))
```

The ordination and magnitude panels run on the missForest-imputed matrix so the
sample sets align; imputation borrows across proteins, which shrinks per-protein
variance and can compress ‖Δ‖. The DEP-derived panels (C–F) use the non-imputed
limma arm.

## Methods note

What each panel claims, the exact statistic, and whether it suits this design. Every
DOI below was resolved against Crossref.

| Panel | Claim | Statistic | Fit to this design |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** state | The proteome does not separate HR from LR at any timepoint | PERMANOVA on the sample × sample distance matrix (Anderson 2001, [10.1046/j.1442-9993.2001.01070.x](https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1442-9993.2001.01070.x)), **`strata = Subject_ID`** | The `strata` argument is doing essential work: it restricts permutations **within subject**, which is what makes the test valid under repeated measures. Without it the 45 samples would be treated as independent and the *p* would be anticonservative. A PCA is shown, but the test is on distances, not on the two plotted axes. |
| **B** magnitude | HR and LR change by the same *amount* | ‖Δ‖ per subject per phase, then RRPP (Collyer & Adams 2018, [10.1111/2041-210x.13029](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210x.13029)), 999 permutations | Correct. Each subject contributes **one** Δ per phase, so the rows are independent and the repeated-measures problem is collapsed away by construction. This is the right way to test a within-subject change between groups. |
| **B** supp | HR and LR change in the same *direction* | Δ-score PCA plus an RRPP vector test and the angle between the two group-mean change vectors | Companion to B: magnitude and direction are separate claims, and both are null. The angle is descriptive (no test on the angle itself). |
| **C** divergence | Candidate proteins whose HR and LR responses part company | π-gated leads (π = p^\|log2FC\|, Xiao et al. 2014, [10.1093/bioinformatics/btr671](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btr671)) | **π is a ranking statistic, not an FDR.** It is fold-change-weighted and is *not* a subset of *p* < 0.05 — `r sprintf("%.1f", min(pi_off_p))`–`r sprintf("%.1f", max(pi_off_p))` % of π-calls have raw *p* ≥ 0.05. **Nothing here survives BH.** The panel is labelled exploratory and must never be read as a discovery list. |
| **C** supp | HR and LR are equally variable | PERMDISP on multivariate dispersion per timepoint (Anderson 2006, [10.1111/j.1541-0420.2005.00440.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1541-0420.2005.00440.x)); per-protein CV scatter on the **linear** scale (Brenes et al. 2019, [10.1074/mcp.ra119.001472](https://doi.org/10.1074/mcp.ra119.001472)) | Reframes replicate variability from QC to biology. CV must be computed on the linear scale, not on log2 — a CV of a log-transformed variable is not interpretable as relative dispersion. |
| **D–F** | Effect-size, DEP-count, and pathway overview | Descriptive distributions and counts from the non-imputed limma arm | Descriptive. The DEP-count panel plots a chance line, which is the honest reference when the counts are at chance. |

**Which matrix, and why it matters.** Panels A, B and their supplements use the
**missForest-imputed** matrix (so every sample has every protein and the distances are
defined); panels C–F use the **non-imputed** limma arm (so no imputed value ever enters a
significance test). Imputation borrows information *across proteins*, which shrinks
per-protein variance and can compress ‖Δ‖ — the direction of that bias is toward the null,
so it does not manufacture the negative result reported here.

**Repeated measures, stated plainly.** 45 samples from 16 subjects is **not** 45
independent observations. Panel A handles this with `strata`; panel B handles it by
reducing each subject to one Δ. Any statistic in this figure that did *neither* would be
anticonservative, and none does.

**Reproducibility.** `geom_jitter()` re-randomises its offsets at render time, so every
jittered layer here is explicitly seeded. Without that, a panel's PNG changes on every
`ggsave` and never reproduces byte-for-byte.

## Key terms

**PERMANOVA** — a permutation test for a difference in multivariate location.
Sensitive to dispersion, so it is read alongside PERMDISP.

**PERMDISP** — tests whether one group is more spread out than the other
(dispersion), the confound PERMANOVA cannot separate on its own.

**RRPP** — permutation of model residuals, the valid scheme when proteins far
outnumber subjects. Used here on one change vector per subject, so nothing is
pseudoreplicated.

**Interaction (Group × Timepoint)** — the correct test of "changes differently in
HR vs LR." Comparing two separate hit lists is not that test.

**pi-gate vs FDR** — the pi-value `p^|log2FC|` ranks by fold-change-weighted
significance but controls no error rate; BH-FDR is the honest bar, and here it
leaves nothing, so the divergent proteins are leads.

## Recap

- Shared global response: PCA/PERMANOVA, RRPP magnitude and direction, and PERMDISP
  all null with subjects as the unit.
- Protein-specific divergence is a pi-gated lead list; no protein survives FDR, so
  the panel reports both counts.
- The one FDR-clean positive is pathway-level (Panel F), and even that is a
  per-contrast count, not a difference test.
